insights.audience_context: Commuters and on-the-go buyers at Dar es Salaam transport stages; household buyers
insights.observation: Dar es Salaam volume grew only because existing home buyers bought more often, while the brand lost 350 ml buyers
insights.contrast: 350 ml versus 1.25 L buyers; cooler versus matched outlets; penetration versus frequency effects
insights.mechanism: The 350 ml purchase is an immediate, on-the-go decision made at the moment a cold drink is available; where cold Fizzi is absent, buyers take a cold competitor or skip
insights.tension: People want a cold drink the moment they step off the bus; Fizzi is often warm or missing at that moment
insights.explanation: Fizzi's growth problem in Dar es Salaam is not loyalty or price: it is losing the on-the-go moment to whoever has the cold bottle there
alternatives: 350 ml buyers moved to other categories (water, juice) for reasons unrelated to cold availability
Panel under-records out-of-home purchases, exaggerating the 350 ml buyer loss
contradictions: Household panel under-records out-of-home purchases, so 350 ml buyer loss may be understated or distorted

confidence.reason: Behavioural panel, a controlled pilot and interviews point the same way; competitor role unmeasured

insights.implication: Recruit and win back buyers through chilled availability at high-footfall on-the-go points, backed by communication of the moment, rather than frequency promotions or premiumisation
insights.validation_need: Phase 1 replication with matched controls; situational retrieval measurement

insights.audience_context: Urban channels, Dar es Salaam and Mwanza
insights.observation: Three annual plans assumed modern trade would reach a quarter of category value; audit share stayed at 14%
insights.mechanism: An unsourced planning sentence was carried forward each year and became treated as fact
insights.explanation: The modern-trade budget shift rests on a repeated assumption that the only category data contradict
alternatives: Audit under-covers new modern trade formats

confidence.reason: Direct audit data over one year; audit coverage limits

insights.implication: Do not move 40% of trade budget to modern trade in 2027

options.title: Win the on-the-go cold moment: chilled 350 ml availability at high-footfall clusters with communications of the moment, on a repaired supply base
options.diagnosis_addressed: Loss of 350 ml on-the-go buyers (INS-B01) and Mwanza availability loss (Demo A)
options.where_to_act: High-footfall dukas and kiosks near transport stages in Dar es Salaam first, then Mwanza once supply is restored
options.how_to_win: Be the cold bottle within reach at the moment of need, and be the brand that comes to mind for it

mechanism.explanation: Chilled availability converts on-the-go moments into purchases, recovering lost 350 ml buyers; communications strengthen retrieval at those moments

options.economics: Phase 1: 180 coolers (TZS 288 million installed plus TZS 45 million a year maintenance). At pilot uplift, payback about 3.1 years; a two-year payback requires outlets with a baseline near 59 litres a week. Scale only after the gate
options.resources: Trade budget for coolers; field team for placement and uptime; communications budget redirected from national weight to cooler clusters
risks: Outlets with high enough baselines are scarce
non_choices: No shift of 40% of trade budget to modern trade
No national cooler roll-out before the Phase 1 gate
conditions: Phase 1 incremental 350 ml sales at least 25 litres a week versus matched controls
Mwanza placements only after distribution recovers (ASM-B03)
reversal_triggers: Phase 1 uplift below 25% versus controls: stop expansion and reassess on-the-go strategy
Situational retrieval research shows Fizzi already leads and uplift is visibility-only: shift spend from communications to placement
options.rationale: Addresses the diagnosed buyer loss with the only lever with controlled evidence; staged and reversible

options.title: Launch a premium Fizzi tier at +30%

mechanism.explanation: Higher price per litre from trading up existing buyers

options.economics: unknown: no willingness-to-pay or premium tier data
options.rationale: No evidence of willingness to pay; core buyer loss is the binding constraint; revisit with a priced test in 2028 if premium tier data justify it

options.title: Drive frequency among existing buyers with 1.25 L family promotions
options.economics: Margin dilution risk on the lowest price-per-litre pack; incremental volume unknown
options.rationale: Frequency is already growing; the constraint is lost buyers; promotions would dilute margin

options.title: Continue the 2026 plan: shift 40% of trade budget to modern trade listings

mechanism.explanation: Presence in a channel assumed to be growing

options.economics: Moves a large share of trade budget into listings (amount depends on the trade budget split, not supplied)
options.rationale: Rests on a repeated assumption contradicted by audit data (INS-B02)

review_flags.reason: Audit shows modern trade share flat at 14% (CLM-B09); assumption was one repeated planning statement (CLM-B08)

options.notes: Reviewed 2026-09-17 after ASM-B01 was refuted: option remains rejected; no further action.
